relevance_note: The paper describes one family with individually labelled TNFAIP3 carriers: 'Two other affected family members (II-4, III-1) were observed to also harbour the mutation, (I-2 is an obligate carrier)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from hand-written values (no table transcription; the paper has no patient table). Four in-scope people: index II-1, II-4, III-1 (daughter of the index) and I-2 (mother of the index, obligate carrier, not stated as tested). Labels are the pedigree labels the paper uses most; the figure legends also call II-1 'patient 1' and III-1 'patient 2'. Ages 30 years (II-1) and 8 years (III-1) come from the figure legends describing the sampled carriers; recorded as age at last evaluation. Sex of II-4 is not stated in text (pedigree drawing not available). Variant printed as 'c.A271T: p.(Lys91*)' with Ensembl IDs ENSG00000118503:ENST00000433680 (non-HGVS cDNA form kept as printed). Variant type (nonsense), zygosity (heterozygous), pathogenicity and functional evidence come from sentences naming this exact variant; for I-2 (obligate carrier, untested) these are left not reported. III-1 inheritance recorded as maternal: she is the daughter of the index II-1, who is a woman and in whom the mutation was confirmed. II-1 inheritance left not reported because her mother I-2 is only an obligate carrier (not tested). II-1's lung finding is 'severe inflammatory lung reaction' in Results and 'severe autoinflammatory lung reaction' in the figure 1 legend (wording difference, not a contradiction); not mapped to interstitial lung disease. Anaemia in II-1 is not stated to be autoimmune, so checklist 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is not reported. Checklist 'skin lesions' marked observed from psoriasis; 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' from atrophic gastritis; 'arthritis or arthralgia' from 'articular symptoms'. Increased circulating IL-18 and cytokine secretion in carrier PBMCs are research assays, recorded only as functional evidence, not as phenotypic features. No contradictions found in the paper.
